request_state.conjecture: Beal: A^x + B^y = C^z with x,y,z >= 3 and gcd(gcd(A,B),C) = 1 has no solutions. Audit has shown three recurring failure modes in this project: conflating a residual mod-p congruence with an isogeny or l-adic statement; using a Chabauty rank bound over a base field to conclude about points of higher degree; and relabelling a GRH-conditional or heuristic result as unconditional.

candidate_A.failure_reason: U96 audit against the primary source found Theorem 5.23 requires Hypothesis 5, which fails identically for the weighted equation. The route is blocked at its stated hypotheses, not merely unfinished.
candidate_A.novelty_note: Records the specific hypothesis failure so the loop does not re-attempt Azon-style level lowering unchanged.
extracted: Hypothesis 5 of Azon Thm 5.23 is the precise failing ingredient: any replacement route must supply level lowering without it
The prime-5 local lift obligation was separately discharged in U98 and is reusable
candidate_A.claim: Level lowering in the style of Azon arXiv:2504.01967v2 Theorem 5.23 applies to the weighted equation X^10 + 256 Y^10 = Z^17 and eliminates the surviving Frey representation.
candidate_A.method: Modular level lowering over a totally real field via Breuil-Diamond Theorem 3.2.2 local lift hypotheses.

obligations: Each of the three obstructions must be independently re-derived from its stated hypotheses alone
The endomorphism algebra dimensions must be confirmed by exact computation, not by table lookup
X_0(17) reducibility step must be checked against a primary source
candidate_B.failure_reason: U113 adversarial audit: all three elimination strategies fail. Strategy 3 refuted by exact computation (its set S of forcing primes is FINITE - exactly {11,31,41,71,131} under the trace criterion for q<1600, with match counts tracking q/17 - so the "positive density / infinitely many" step is false; Deligne equidistribution argues against the claim, not for it; it also conflates U68/U72 Gaussian-valuation forcing primes with mod-17 Frobenius congruence primes, and misapplies Baker superelliptic bounds to a three-term equation). Strategy 2 is circular: R=T does not turn a residual mod-17 isomorphism into a characteristic-zero isogeny, and if it did the modular method would need no elimination step at all; its endomorphism-dimension contradiction is therefore vacuous. Strategy 1 is a category error: J^- is an abelian surface with RM, so an O_K-linear 17-isogeny is classified by a Hilbert modular variety, not by the elliptic modular curve X_0(17); the cited Momose/Darmon-Merel/Bilu-Parent-Rebolledo statements are not quoted with their actual hypotheses and do not cover M=Q(zeta_5).
candidate_B.novelty_note: Claimed unconditional but not yet adversarially audited; status is deliberately VERIFICATION_REQUIRED rather than PROVED.
extracted: disc(f)=2^24*5^5*Z^68 VERIFIED symbolically and at 5 exact specialisations; good reduction at every q|Y stands
orbit b ~ Jac(C_0)/K VERIFIED by point counting: (S,P)=(9,19),(-11,29),(-1,-151) at q=11,31,41 and a_q=0 for q not=1 mod 5
the mod-17 split sieve is FINITE with forcing set {11,31,41,71,131} for q<1600 - a genuine finite obstruction, usable but not inflatable to an infinitude argument
Gaussian-valuation forcing primes (U68/U72) and mod-17 Frobenius forcing primes (U97) are DIFFERENT sets and must not be conflated
candidate_B.claim: The Hilbert newform orbit b at level 2000 (2.2.5.1-2000.1-b) is eliminated unconditionally, so no surviving newform orbit supports the weighted-equation Frey representation.
candidate_B.method: Three independent global obstructions: reducibility over Q(zeta_5) via X_0(17); endomorphism dimension clash dim End^0(J^-) = 2 != 4 = dim End^0(Jac(C_0)); R = T deformation rigidity against the boundary CM curve C_0: y^2 = 64 - x^5.

compatible.instructions: Are these two research candidates mathematically COMPATIBLE, in the sense that the objects, fields, exponents and equations they concern are the same or are related by a reduction that the project has already proved?

criteria.true: they concern the same equation, signature, curve or field, or one supplies an input the other consumes
criteria.false: they concern unrelated equations, signatures or methods, so no joint statement could be formed without inventing a new reduction

combination_value.instructions: If these two candidates were combined into a single line of attack, how much would the combination accomplish beyond what the better of the two accomplishes alone?
criteria: level 0: nothing; the combination is just the stronger candidate restated, or they are incompatible
level 1: the combination tidies bookkeeping but resolves no obligation that either one leaves open
level 2: one candidate discharges a specific open obligation recorded in the other
level 3: the combination closes a case or an infinite family that neither one closes alone

shared_failure.instructions: Would these two candidates FAIL FOR THE SAME REASON, so that combining them adds no diversity of failure mechanism and a single obstruction would defeat both?

criteria.true: both depend on the same blocked step, the same unverified citation, or the same one of the three recorded failure modes
criteria.false: they would fail for different reasons, so each provides genuine independent information
